Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **TV static**: the new `static` flip type draws moving static over the scene, for a broken screen, a bad signal or a memory breaking up, on a KAG layer (`[image layer=1 flip=static visible=true opacity=96]`) or a World layer (`[newlay name=tv static=tv]`), with a grain size, colour, a rolling band and scanlines to choose (`doc/kagex.txt`, "Optional parameters for static"). `level=message` puts a World layer over the message window too, under the save, load and config screens, and the window's buttons still work under the static
- **Pitch and pan for World music and sounds**: `[bgm pitch=35 time=2500]` slows the music down like a tape running out, and `[se name=se_steps pan=100 time=3000]` moves a sound from left to right; saves keep them (`doc/world.txt`, "BGM Object Functions" and "SE Object Functions"). The Effects demo ends with both
- **kagex-release fixes**: rule images stay PNG in a TLG or JPEG build (the engine can't use a TLG as a rule, so those transitions became crossfades); your `krkrz.cf` options reach the Android, iOS and web builds too; a script with `(const)` arrays or dictionaries stays as source when scripts are compiled (they read as null otherwise); Android builds on Windows find the APK they made in a deep folder; a folder Windows holds for a moment is removed on a retry
- **Framework fixes**: a menu caption `&File` shows as `File`; a movie named without its extension finds its `.webm`; `[se name=...]` no longer tries to play a file called "name"
- kagex-release 0.15.0 downloads the 0.15.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.15.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
